dimensions.assessment: Affects state regulatory authorities, electric utilities, and utility customers in states with intermittent energy policies.
dimensions.evidence: Each State regulatory authority that implements an intermittent energy policy shall conduct, and make publicly available, a general evaluation

dimensions.assessment: Imposes administrative and reporting requirements on state regulatory bodies rather than directly changing energy policies or rates itself.
dimensions.evidence: conduct, and make publicly available, a general evaluation of... the effects of implementing the intermittent energy policy on the reliability of the bulk-power system

dimensions.assessment: No federal spending or revenue effects are stated or implied.
Amends federal utility law (PURPA) to add a new mandatory evaluation standard for state regulators.
dimensions.evidence: To amend the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to add a standard related to the evaluation of State intermittent energy policies

dimensions.assessment: Establishes a permanent statutory evaluation standard, requiring state determinations and public reports within specified timeframes.
dimensions.evidence: each State regulatory authority shall consider and make a determination concerning whether it is appropriate to implement the standard... not later than 1 year after the date of enactment

missing_information: The number of states currently maintaining qualifying intermittent energy policies that must perform the evaluation is not enumerated.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill amends the Public Utility Regulatory Policies Act of 1978 to require state regulatory authorities that implement intermittent energy policies to conduct and publicly release evaluations of their effects on grid reliability, rates, and emergency capacity.
